Variable stars hold a pivotal position in the broader astronomy community, serving as reference points to measure precise distances and rotation rates of celestial objects. To effectively classify variable stars, it is essential to have an accurate estimation of their periods. In this research, we examine the reliability of period estimates from the Kepler and K2 missions by conducting a comprehensive analysis of 1564 sources with a known period. Our study reveals that the period estimates derived from the Pipock and Pirc standards of the Kepler and K2 missions exhibit a 1.8% and 1.5% relative error on average, respectively. Moreover, we discover that the primary factors contributing to these discrepancies are the presence of noise in period estimates and the variability in period measurement precision across different types of sources.

This study presents a method for creating stable and flexible control systems of any order, based on a specific system model (NIBSS) that can handle disturbances and uncertainties. A simple approach to monitoring these systems is developed, involving a single adjustable parameter that can be easily determined. This enables the real-time detection of control system failures caused by malfunctions, disturbances, or other factors. The proposed method is successfully applied to the control and monitoring of a complex robotic arm.

Human cognition is known to be susceptible to a phenomenon known as cognitive overload, where exposure to an abundance of information can disrupt existing knowledge and lead to memory loss. Interestingly, recent studies in artificial intelligence have demonstrated a similar phenomenon called catastrophic forgetting, where models lose previously acquired skills due to training on new tasks. Despite these findings, it remains unclear whether these AI models truly learn in an increasingly complex manner. To investigate this, researchers conducted an experiment using a neural network with a basic learning capability. They found that when the model is exposed to new information, it initially causes forgetting, but also leads to an increase in its ability to generalize across different scenarios. These results suggest that overfitting, a well-studied problem in machine learning, can have a more intricate impact on AI systems than previously thought.

In environments where people speak multiple languages, informal communication frequently incorporates code-switching, switching between different languages in mid-sentence. To better understand this phenomenon, we created and released the first publicly available English-Hindi code-switched text dataset, intended for use in modeling and generation. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of various language models, both standalone and in combination with other models, in predicting the next word in a sentence that switches languages. We also propose a novel method for enhancing low-resource language modeling in such scenarios.

This lecture will be easy to follow for those with basic physics knowledge. It will address three longstanding particle physics and cosmology mysteries: the universe's mass, why the Higgs particle leads to the universe's mass, and the lack of detectable dark matter particles. Introducing new concepts of symmetry groups and their applications to particle physics will be a necessary element in solving these puzzles. It is intended that students gain a deeper understanding of the underlying principles rather than a comprehensive review.

Web applications heavily rely on user input to trigger notifications, and key performance metrics, such as the number of unopened notifications, depend on how users interact with them. Accurately predicting user responses is crucial for any web application and has far-reaching implications for both business efficiency and user engagement. Existing models used to predict user responses have several limitations, and a novel deep learning approach is needed to effectively address these shortcomings. This paper introduces a novel framework that leverages the capabilities of deep learning models to improve the prediction of user responses, and it is demonstrated on a real-world dataset from a prominent email marketing company. The results show that deep learning models significantly outperform traditional models used for this purpose, and our approach provides valuable insights into the underlying data distribution.

Cell-free networks with intelligent reflecting surfaces have shown great potential in improving system capabilities. Building on previous research, this study examines the optimal design of such networks in terms of user data rates. It formulates rate constraints using a recently developed method, and then uses them to develop upper and lower bounds on the minimum required number of surfaces. To validate these bounds, this study analyzes the impact of surface placement on network performance, and identifies a critical factor that affects the effectiveness of these surfaces. Additionally, this research investigates the benefits of using surfaces in terms of reduced transmission power, and provides insights into their potential benefits. Finally, it presents numerical results to validate the findings and discuss practical considerations for deploying such systems.

To enhance prediction accuracy in branch prediction, a method has been devised that uses deep learning methods, built upon the principles of supervised learning. A new approach, though, has been devised to counter the adverse effects of training data bias, achieved through the incorporation of an ensemble classifier. This technique, known as the Ensemble Classifier for Bias Reduction (ECBR), utilizes an ensemble of weak classifiers, working together in a boosting framework to create a robust prediction model, on which various machine learning algorithms can be trained to forecast branch outcomes. The proposed method, called EC-BP, integrates ECBR into the branch prediction module, resulting in improved prediction accuracy across different applications, notably those with infrequently taken branches. The efficiency of the proposed ECB-BP method is further amplified by employing a hardware-friendly quantized variant known as Quant-ECB-BP. The evaluation of the proposed technique demonstrates a significant improvement in branch prediction accuracy, measured by mean squared error (MSE), across 14 diverse benchmarks, resulting in an average reduction of prediction errors by 8.5%.

In the context of visual active monitoring for surveillance and traffic applications, agents must identify and respond to relevant visual events in real-time, enhancing their performance through the use of both visual and textual cues and a human guidance mechanism called imitation learning. Imitation learning allows agents to absorb and learn from human actions in a previously unseen environment, and it can be combined with the existing reinforcement learning-based active monitoring framework to incorporate human behavior into an agent's knowledge. By leveraging both visual and textual information to learn and act in an environment, agents can better comprehend and replicate human behavior, thereby resulting in more precise and efficient visual active monitoring.

In the SOS model on a Cayley tree, multiple solutions have been discovered for the boundary law, with these solutions characterized by their regularity and divergence. We've found that the regular solution exhibits a specific type of stability, while the divergent solution exhibits a scale-invariant form. Notably, one of these solutions has yet to be identified in earlier studies. The SOS model with the regular boundary solution exhibits a phase transition, with critical temperatures reaching a maximum when this solution is applied in an infinite tree. Interestingly, when applied in an infinite tree, the divergent boundary solution leads to a system existing in a single state of equilibrium.

The interaction of a time-entangled photon pair with a two-level system can be seen as a quantum-mechanical extension of energy transfer via classical light, offering new insights into this process. Our research focuses on the influence of temporal entanglement on energy transfer, revealing its capacity to modulate the frequency correlation of photons and the resulting impact on transferred energy. Notably, we discovered that the sign of the entanglement contributes significantly to the direction of energy transfer. Additionally, we observed a distinct shift in the peak position of the transferred energy when compared to the case of time-uncorrelated photons. Our findings provide a deeper understanding of the potential for quantum control in quantum-radiation-based applications of quantum electrodynamics.

Within the context of light-cone QCD sum rules, our analysis provides estimates for the strong coupling constants of the charmed and bottom mesons, specifically those interacting with the heavy mesons, involving $J/\psi$ and $\Upsilon$. This investigation also takes into account both scalar and vector types of interactions. Our results are then compared with those from various theoretical models and the available experimental data.

The detection of matter-breakout neutrinos from the core collapse of massive stars holds significant promise for neutrino physics research. Specifically, the DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokandre experiments aim to investigate key aspects, including the neutrino oscillations, the neutrino-electron scattering, and the behavior of neutrinos in the presence of matter. Moreover, these initiatives will provide a more precise determination of the neutrino mass hierarchy, as well as the matter-antimatter asymmetry within the core collapse supernovae.

A fundamental challenge in observational studies is mitigating confounding variables to draw inferences comparable to a controlled experimental design.  The use of propensity score methods offers a reliable means of achieving balance for observed covariates.  This study examines the application of a data-driven approach based on Support Vector Machines (SVM) to enhance linear regression models for balancing covariates.  By incorporating SVM coefficients into the regression model, the resulting data-driven weights can be used for covariate adjustment.  The performance of the data-driven weights is compared to a standard propensity score approach in a synthetic observational study under different sampling designs and data reduction strategies.  The results indicate that the data-driven weights can effectively reduce covariate imbalance across a range of designs and models, producing comparable estimates of treatment effects to the standard method.

This study presents a non-model-based damping control approach for power systems. The proposed control method, which combines droop control and pole placement, does not require knowledge of system model parameters or dynamics. It effectively regulates inter-area oscillations without any restrictions related to network geometry or controller distribution. The control method, which is adaptable to changing network conditions, utilizes real-time network parameters obtained from monitoring the network's admittance matrix. The effectiveness of this control method is demonstrated through small and large disturbances in the IEEE 68-bus and 118-bus systems. The study highlights the benefits of this control method in terms of stability and robustness.

We investigate the phenomenon of simultaneous decay of a pair of atoms from their initial, metastable state to two lower, stable states in close proximity. This process is realized through a multi-level scheme consisting of two $7s$ or $8s$ excited atoms, with their lower states being in the $6p$, $7p$, or $8p$ orbitals. The interaction between the atoms is represented by a variable, effective, van der Waals coefficient, which is influenced by the distance between the atoms. The probability of simultaneous decay is determined by the overlap of the two decay amplitudes, with the first atom decaying to the first, lower state and the second to the second, lower state. This research reveals that the collective radiation emitted by the ensemble is diminished when the two atoms decay simultaneously, with the suppression of radiation being more pronounced as the distance between the atoms decreases. Furthermore, we observe that the ensemble exhibits a notable, long-lived, coherent memory effect, which persists for a time period comparable to the natural lifetime of the ensemble's collective radiative states. This research has implications for the development of a new, two-atom, laser-based, interferometric technique for measuring the separation between atoms, which is relevant to the investigation of the Pauli adiabatic principle in quantum systems.

We provide a condition, similar to Makhlov's, to determine whether a small odd perturbation of the kink solution of the $\phi^4$ equation leads to a stable, asymptotically stable, or unstable time-periodic solution. Specifically, we examine the long-term behavior under odd perturbations for kinks with negative stability of the internal mode.

The NT23 experiment at JLab investigated final-state color transparency (CT) in hadrons undergoing high-energy collisions. CT occurs when hadrons initially interact extremely quickly, reducing their color charge over time through gluon emission. Researchers analyzed the CT effect in $\Lambda$ hyperons created from the high-energy collisions of protons and deuterons. They measured the time it takes for the $\Lambda$'s polarization to relax and the resulting angular distributions, allowing them to determine the $\Lambda$'s production point using the polarization dependence. These findings align with theoretical predictions based on CT and gluon emission models.

This research introduces an innovative consistency training technique that encourages models to produce similar output predictions for varying input variations, specifically modifications to image feature maps, while preserving the original image data. Our approach is grounded in the understanding that, given two images, the corresponding representations within a convolutional neural network can serve as a suitable alternative to the original images. Our proposed method enhances the robustness of models by equipping them with the ability to make accurate predictions on modified images. Experimental evaluations on the ImageNet and CIFAR-10 datasets confirm the efficacy of our approach.

In gastrointestinal endoscopy, detecting polyps through visual inspection is a critical yet challenging task.  Although deep learning-based approaches have been explored for localizing polyps in endoscopy videos, they are hindered by issues like significant frame-to-frame variations and optical artifacts.  A recent study developed a video attention-guided convolutional learning framework, known as VAGCL, which effectively addresses these problems.  VAGCL framework leverages a novel video attention module that identifies crucial segments within polyp videos and guides a convolutional learning module in modeling efficient features.  By incorporating the attention module, VAGCL bypasses the challenges associated with inter-frame variations and artifacts.  Evaluations conducted on a large, publicly available polyp video dataset show that VAGCL outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches in localization accuracy.  VAGCL achieved an impressive mean average precision of 0.89 and a high Fowlkes Minkowski similarity of 0.73 on a benchmark dataset.  Additionally, the proposed video attention model provides a more accurate and robust polyp segmentation method, which can be applied to other video-based segmentation tasks.

A novel sampling approach utilizing sequential inference and adaptive likelihood ratio tests has been developed for selecting equal-sized distinct samples without replacement from a large dataset. This technique relies on a modified form of the unequal probability sampling method initially proposed by Demessemaker (1964). By applying a sliding window and dynamically adjusting the sample size based on the observed data, the proposed scheme seeks to minimize the risk of selecting multiple occurrences of a particular data value. This is achieved by setting an upper limit on the number of repetitions allowed for each data value within each sampling window. By applying a series of likelihood ratio tests to each window, the sample is sequentially constructed by adding one observation at a time. This method's effectiveness is evaluated through simulations using artificial data sets, revealing that the method's performance is comparable to that of the optimal sampling approach when the optimal sample size is employed, while outperforming other baseline methods when the optimal sample size is unknown.

We have conducted a beta decay study of $^{57}$Zn using the TPC, employing the $\beta$-delayed proton emission of $^{58}$Cu. This study utilized the SPECTTRUM array at RIKEN, where $^{58}$Cu was created through the fusion of $^{28}$Mg and $^{30}$S. We employed a magnetic spectrometer to detect protons and a large silicon detector array for $\gamma$-rays to measure the $\beta$-delayed proton emission of $^{58}$Cu. This study allowed us to determine the $\beta$-delayed proton emission spectrum of $^{58}$Cu and provided insight into the $^{57}$Zn half-life. Furthermore, our findings have enabled the determination of the $^{57}$Zn ground state spin to be less than $\frac{5}{2}^{+}$.

We have established a generalization of the Manin-Mumford theorem for abelian schemes over rings of integers, along with various corollaries that reveal the intricacies of special points in families of abelian varieties over integers.

Pulsars are remarkable astrophysical objects shedding light on extreme conditions found in the universe. They accelerate particles to incredibly high energies via a pulsar wind, influencing surrounding interstellar medium and forming complex structures such as pulsar wind nebulae. These structures emit across the electromagnetic spectrum, providing valuable insights into pulsars and associated particle acceleration processes. This review discusses various pulsar wind nebulae observed in different wavelengths, focusing on the role of acceleration mechanisms and environmental factors that shape these structures.

This paper's primary objective is to analyze the long-term behavior of the solutions to a specific class of reaction-diffusion equations within an attractor framework. We draw upon the analytical properties of the underlying theory, particularly those associated with the semigroup generated by the system's parabolic operator. We establish that the system's global attractor consists of equations representing the long-term behavior of the original reaction-diffusion equation. As a consequence, we are also able to establish the existence of the long-time behavior of the original reaction-diffusion equation and its associated semigroup.

The discovery of ultra-compact dwarf galaxies (UCDs) and globular clusters (GCs) is significant for understanding the formation of galaxies. UCDs and GCs are crucial for studying the effects of feedback from active galactic nuclei (AGN), their chemical properties, and the role of feedback from massive stars. UCDs and GCs are crucial tracers in understanding galaxy evolution, including mergers and interactions between galaxies. Despite their importance, UCDs and GCs are still not well understood in the context of galaxy evolution, particularly in the context of feedback and the role of AGN. A recent study of the galaxy M101 has provided new insights into UCDs and GCs, including their metallicity and the role of feedback from supernovae. The study also found that metal-rich UCDs and GCs have similar properties, and that metal-poor UCDs and GCs have different properties. The study also found that metal-rich UCDs and GCs have different properties, and that metal-poor UCDs and GCs have different properties, suggesting that metallicity plays a significant role in the formation of these objects. The study also found that metal-rich UCDs and GCs have different properties, and that metal-poor UCDs and GCs have different properties, suggesting that metallicity plays a significant role in the formation of these objects.

The field of Recommender Systems (RS) has undergone significant transformation
over the past few decades, affecting not only our daily lives but also global
commerce and communication. As a result, the demand for tailored recommendations has become more pressing. However, developing accurate and engaging recommendations remains a daunting task due to the complexity of user behavior patterns and preferences. This article aims to provide a comprehensive overview of RS models, starting with a historical examination of RS systems and tools before exploring advanced models and evaluation methods. Furthermore, we will discuss the application of RS in various systems, such as content recommendation, and highlight the unique challenges of the research field. Additionally, we will discuss the current research trends, outstanding issues, and potential directions.

This study investigates the asymptotic behavior of the generalized one-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov test when dealing with heavy-tailed distributions. The asymptotic properties of the test are analyzed in the context of the norm of the empirical process, considering the possibility of truncated test statistics. The results show that the asymptotic distribution of the test is normal when certain conditions are met, specifically when the tail index is greater than 1/2 and a specific condition known as Cram\'er condition is satisfied. The research also explores the case of alpha-stable distributions where the tail index is greater than or equal to 1/2.

A significant advancement in technology has enabled non-invasive control of robotic arms and prosthetic limbs through Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI). However, current methods based on electroencephalogram (EEG) signals struggle to accurately interpret complex brain commands, often resulting in incorrect or sluggish movements. Our study introduces an innovative approach that addresses these issues through a multi-stage classification process, utilizing a mid-level representation to enhance tokenization of EEG signals. This technique has been successfully applied to a real-world application - guiding a prosthetic hand to pick objects from a table. Our results demonstrate a notable improvement in EEG decoding with a high accuracy of 65.32% on a specific dataset.

We've developed a novel method to calculate a critical two-point function in 3-dimensional conformal field theories, with test cases focusing on scalars and fermions. This approach is built on advanced techniques from generalized Kontsevich-Zakopene formulas and the method of harmonic analysis. Although our method is general, its explicit evaluation is often restricted to specific conditions due to the high complexity of the involved integrals. Consequently, we apply a technique known as the method of principal series to provide a simplified result for certain spin values of $\phi$ within the test class of scalars.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants is the incompatibility between the donor and the recipient due to mismatched antibodies. Desensitization through the use of immunosuppressive therapy is a viable approach to overcome this incompatibility, allowing life-saving kidney transplants to take place for patients in need. We have developed a comprehensive model that simulates kidney transplant waiting lists for patients with highly urgent medical requirements. Our model accounts for the complex trade-offs involved in transplant matching protocols. By analyzing the waiting lists of patients with two transplant options, we have identified the most effective strategies for minimizing waiting times and the number of patients on waiting lists while considering the distinct challenges faced by patients receiving desensitized transplants. Our analysis reveals that prioritizing patients for desensified transplants results in lower average wait times, especially for patients with highly urgent medical requirements, even though this strategy does not address the unique challenges faced by patients receiving desensified transplants. We have also found that this strategy results in a significant improvement in waiting times for patients with highly urgent medical requirements of at least 10% in comparison to the current approach.

This study investigates the computational efficiency of Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods in estimating hidden parameters of statistical models used for predicting time series and sequential data. We assess the accuracy of MCMC estimators compared to maximum likelihood estimators through a comprehensive simulation study focusing on Hidden Markov Models and their generalization, the Long Short-Term Memory model. Our research reveals notable differences in predictive accuracy between MCMC estimators and maximum likelihood estimators. Moreover, we examine the influence of sample size, model complexity, and simulation variability on these discrepancies.

This research examines the boundedness, compactness, and strong summability of generalized Volterra integral operators within the context of certain weighted normed spaces related to Orlicz sequences.

Experience management, a growing business field, focuses on creating and tracking individual experiences. Due to the high cost and difficulty in replicating experiences, businesses seek to personalise offers to specific individuals based on their past experiences. Research in machine learning has made significant progress in addressing this issue. Our study aims to improve upon current experience modeling methods, which typically focus on a single task at a time, by developing a multi-task model capable of processing various types of data formats, including missing and imbalanced data. Through five applications in experience management, we show that our approach outperforms current methods while reducing model memory usage.

In high energy physics, open data drives scientific advancement and innovation alike. The CERN Open Data project aims to offer tangible data usage examples, fostering a culture where open data can be shared, utilized, and created. Through the following case studies, we demonstrate the value of open data: (a) creating a publicly accessible LHC dataset, (b) a data platform supporting the LHCf and TOTEM experiments, (c) developing two open source physics detectors, and (d) establishing a dataset for particle physics, "OpenDataMDA." Additionally, this study outlines the CODA project's self-imposed constraints and the CERN Architecture for AI's impact on shaping the project's guidelines.

We've developed a new method to break down complex Richelot isogenies into simpler components, leveraging properties of Richelot isogeny graphs and the isogeny dilation factor. This breakthrough enables us to efficiently generate a wide range of decomposed isogenies and identify the underlying patterns within them. Furthermore, our work has led to the creation of a comprehensive graph illustrating the relationships between these newly discovered isogeny families.

Recent discoveries of hot subdwarfs with strong magnetic fields have raised questions about the prevalence of magnetism within this stellar group. A comprehensive study of 12 hot subdwarfs observed by the Magellan/SPecs spectrograph has provided substantial evidence that a significant proportion of hot subdwarfs possess strong magnetic fields. The analysis found that at least 11 of the observed stars exhibited magnetism, with field strengths exceeding 5000 Gauss and rotation periods of approximately 1.5 to 10 hours. The results suggest that a minimum of 40% of hot subdwarfs possess strong magnetic fields, with an estimated minimum strength of 100 Gauss, and a maximum prevalence of at least 65% of hot subdwarfs exhibiting magnetism.

In many statistical and machine learning applications, matrices with specific properties such as positive semi-definiteness or low-rankness play a significant role. To address this need, a new minimization technique has been developed to enhance the eigenvalue condition number of a near-positive semi-definite matrix. This is achieved by iteratively applying an optimized convex function to specific matrix components. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through its ability to produce well-performing outcomes in simple and complex cases, leading to improved numerical performance such as faster linear system solvers. The algorithm's efficiency is further reinforced by its low computational requirements which are independent of the matrix size.

Wikipedia's content is presented in a multi-layered format, utilizing a combination of text and multimedia elements. The balanced representation of information, which includes the use of images, tables, and other multimedia tools, is achieved through the use of HTML markup. Historically, Wikipedia analyses have been conducted by examining the underlying text-based template system and natural language, with limited consideration for the role of visual elements. The authors of this study propose a novel methodology that leverages the power of HTML to derive comprehensive information from the Wikipedia dataset. The newly developed method allows for the creation of a vast array of meaningful features that can be used to represent Wikipedia's textual content. The newly designed feature set is applied to a variety of tasks, such as predicting user satisfaction, article deletion, and language identification. The results demonstrate that this novel approach to feature engineering achieves better performance compared to traditional methods, with significant improvements in the cases of article deletion and language identification.

Recent discoveries have highlighted the potential of twisted bilayers formed from electronic structure symmetry between layers, such as observed in $\mathbf{B}$-doped graphene and WSe$_2$, as anemometer sensors. The creation of these twisted bilayers relies heavily on the symmetry breaking of the two layers' spin-orbit-induced polarizations, which can be explained by our developed model. This model, which can be applied to any twisted pair of low-dimensional systems, shows that the magnitude of the polarization components is directly proportional to the twist angle and the symmetry difference between the layers' spin-orbit coupling. The model also predicts that the ratio of the perpendicular polarization components will be a fixed value, approximately $\frac{\sin^2(2\theta_0)}{\cos^2(2\theta_0)}$ for a specific angle $\theta_0$, which can be used to determine the twist angle of the bilayer. The model's predictions are further validated by examining the polarization patterns in $\text{MoSe}_2$ and $\text{TaS}_2$ bilayers.

The assumption that our universe is flat and homogeneous may soon be thoroughly examined by upcoming observational evidence.  Groundbreaking tests of general relativity and advanced cosmological measurements will soon offer precise, multiproduct evidence.  New analysis techniques will be developed to efficiently analyze large datasets from multiple cosmic sources, such as supernovae, gravitational wave data, and large-scale structure findings.  These studies will provide crucial insights into the universe's spatial structure and the behavior of gravity, allowing us to refine our understanding of the universe and its fundamental laws.  Specifically, this research will investigate the implications of recent findings regarding the spatial structure of the universe and identify potential new avenues for improving our understanding of gravity.  Additionally, this research will explore the capabilities and limitations of upcoming multiproduct analysis tools and identify potential research avenues for improving these methods.  Ultimately, this research will outline the key advancements and challenges for future cosmological studies.

The unique characteristics of the optical phenomenon known as the Madelbrot bubble, observed when colloidal particles are in a state of metastable motion within nematic liquid crystals, are investigated. A theoretical model is developed to quantify the local energy patterns driving colloidal particle movement in confined nematic environments. By analyzing the energy signatures of particle confinement, our model reveals that the energy landscape is influenced by both particle size and environment geometry. This analysis allows us to determine the stability of metastable particle configurations and their susceptibility to disturbances. Notably, our theoretical predictions are in agreement with the energy patterns measured experimentally, and our model provides a tool for interpreting and designing stable particle arrangements. This study offers new insights into the underlying physical principles governing colloidal particle arrangements in confined nematic environments.

We've developed a tool that allows us to study how an asteroid's surface changes under extreme gravitational stress caused by a close planetary encounter. This tool uses detailed physical models to calculate the variations in the asteroid's shape, based on the principles of gravity and elasticity. We found that longer, more irregularly shaped asteroids experience more significant differences in their surface slopes, with the maximum differences occurring at lower speeds and deeper gravitational deformation. The shape of an asteroid changes more significantly near its equator than at its poles. The orientation of an asteroid's axis also affects its surface, with the axis parallel to the planetary body causing the least variation and at 45 degrees causing the most. When comparing the findings of our study to a similar research approach, we found that longer, more irregularly shaped asteroids experience more significant differences in their surface, with the average difference in surface slope increasing by 0.5-0.9 degrees for each 0.1-0.2 increase in shape elongation and each 10 degree decrease in axis tilt. The maximum depth of gravitational deformation also plays a significant role, with the average difference in surface slope increasing by 0.1-0.2 degrees for each 10 degree increase in gravitational stress. The findings of our study can be applied to real-world asteroid scenarios, such as the case of (216) Kleopatra, a small asteroid that has an unusually high density and highly irregular shape.

Complex biological systems exhibit spontaneous structural changes that play a key role in their function and dynamics. A significant computational challenge in this context is identifying these changes in detailed simulations of complex systems. A new method has been developed to detect and correct corrections in large simulations of complex biological systems. This method uses a data-driven approach to build a statistical model of the system from data and then applies it to correct errors and identify rare events. The results show that the method can effectively detect and correct corrections in detailed simulations of a complex biological system.

The causes behind the high-energy radiation and particle acceleration in powerful jet-emitters such as quasars, gamma-ray bursts, and active galactic nuclei are still unknown. Measuring the polarization of radiation from these sources can provide valuable insights, as it can indicate the presence of magnetic fields and move in concurrence with the jet's axis. A new method for measuring the polarization of high-energy gamma rays emitted by these sources has been developed, utilizing the spatial distribution of excess polarized photons. This method has been applied to the blazar 3C 279, which has been monitored by the H.E.S.S. telescope since 2004. The results show that 3C 279's high-energy gamma-ray emission exhibits significant polarization, reaching up to 25% in certain intervals, and that these measurements are in line with the idea that the jet's magnetic field is aligned with its axis. This study demonstrates that a large number of sources can be analyzed for polarization using the developed method, and it will be applied to a comprehensive list of sources in the future.

We investigate the change in ice thickness distribution, denoted as $g(h)$, with respect to in situ ice thickness $h$. Our analysis reveals a pattern where $g(h)$ consistently shifts towards smaller values as the ice thickness decreases. Specifically, we find that the ice thickness distribution, particularly for young ice, can be accurately represented by a two-parameter Weibull function when the ice thickness is above a certain threshold, but switches to a one-parameter exponential function when the ice thickness falls below that threshold.

In this study, we identify the generalized Weierstrass semigroup at specific points on curves of type $\mathcal{X}_{a,b,c,s,e,h,l}$, as well as its generalization, $\mathcal{X}_{a,b,c,s,e,h,l}^{(n, m)}$. This investigation originates in the analysis of the algebraic curves with Picard exceptional lines, where a relationship is established between exceptional lines and Weierstrass semigroups.

Over the past ten years, there has been significant progress in the creation of singing voices generated by text. Various systems have been created to produce natural-sounding voices, and the development of deep learning algorithms has greatly improved the quality of text-to-speech conversion. This survey will cover the most advanced techniques for producing multiple voices from a single text, utilize standard voice synthesis methods, and examine the most effective algorithms for generating phoneme-level singing texts. It will also discuss the challenges and the most promising directions for improving the growth of text-to-singing synthesis technology.

The task of identifying and classifying bird sounds in real-world environments is a significant challenge, made more complex by the scarcity of large datasets featuring complete bird recordings. To address this issue, we've created a vast audio repository known as BirdRLP, comprising over 1,000 hours of fully annotated recordings, each with detailed information about the bird's location and type. This dataset was used to train a cutting-edge machine learning model, allowing it to classify bird calls and species in real-time using audio clips. When put to the test in a multi-label setting, our model was able to recognize bird sounds with 40% accuracy, outperforming existing techniques by 5-10%.

We introduce a versatile event camera calibration system that can operate in diverse environments, including those with intense light. This system utilizes a neural network to analyze image reconstructions created through machine learning, allowing it to accurately calibrate event cameras across various scenes. Unlike traditional calibration systems, our system is not hindered by reflective surfaces as it relies solely on optical properties. Furthermore, our approach eliminates the need for intricate optical systems, instead using a single layer that handles the task efficiently. Experiments have demonstrated that this method produces accurate intrinsic parameters and is robust against external factors.

Graph learning involves working with graph data structures that incorporate node information. Unlike standard tabular data, this requires considering the interconnections between nodes. As a result, LSTMs have become a preferred method for graph data, but they come with two primary limitations. Firstly, LSTMs' hidden state allows for infinite information storage, which can lead to overfitting issues. Secondly, LSTMs require additional memory to store node representations. To address these issues, this study proposes a unique graph-to-text method. It converts graph data into a text-based representation consisting of node and edge descriptions, utilizing a pre-trained BERT model. Experimental results show the method achieves competitive results with models having access to node and edge information when these are not available.

We have compiled a list of exceptional plane curves related to weak del Pezzo surfaces, with an algorithm for generating them and an estimate of their numbers. These exceptional curves serve as the foundation for constructing canonical thickenings of the surfaces, and we demonstrate that the resulting three-dimensional canonical rings are finite over the surface's canonical ring with respect to a specific ideal.

This study introduces a novel image-guided robot-assisted surgery system specifically designed for retinal procedures. A 3D high-definition live view of the retina is achieved through the use of indocyanine green enhanced ocular fundus imaging. The research outlines a sophisticated navigation system that tracks the surgeon's tools in 3D real-time and the intraocular lens. The navigation system is used in conjunction with a vision-guided task system that assists in positioning and orienting instruments during delicate retinal surgeries. The research also evaluates the accuracy of the navigation system by comparing it with post-operative fundus photographs. The system is successfully tested in a series of simulated virtual scenarios and demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed approach.

We explore F-polynomials within cluster algebras and their inherent properties. By utilizing F-polynomials, we establish a formula for the mutation class of a quiver's cluster variables. Additionally, we establish a connection between F-polynomials and broken curves, ultimately deriving a combinatorial description of F-polynomials. This leads to a description of F-polynomials as complex interlacing permutations, conditional on specific dynamics following a quiver's symmetry change.

The integration of FIDO2, a relatively new technology, marks a significant milestone toward 'passwordless authentication,' but we argue that the internet sector has already reached a point of no return; traditional passwords can never be eradicated entirely. To support this claim, we present a series and interconnected chain of difficult situations that any solution attempting to completely abolish passwords on the web would need to confront. These challenges pertain to issues involving user experience, security, user protection, and regulatory compliance, as well as addressing the pushback from various stakeholders with conflicting interests. To validate our assertion, we conducted an in-depth examination of Google's push for passwordless authentication on its Chrome OS platform, where we discovered that the company is taking a more nuanced approach: instead of fully abandoning passwords, they are developing a hybrid system that blends traditional passwords with passwordless protocols.

We present a novel method to construct a deformed canonical transformation, enabling the transformation of a discrete lattice model into a continuous momentum space. Unlike existing methods, this transformation does not rely on compacting the lattice and can accommodate arbitrary initial momentum ranges. Furthermore, this approach offers an unexplored avenue for modifying traditional lattice thermodynamics by allowing for the introduction of novel momentum-dependent terms in the Hamiltonian.

The video app industry, primarily driven by YouTube, has been incredibly successful,
not only in revenue, but also in shaping the way we consume media. However, the
industry's methods of engagement often come at a cost, creating conflicts of interest
between user experience and provider profit. One of the most contentious features,
autoplay, has been widely criticized for its negative impact on user autonomy and well-being,
prompting an examination of the industry's practices. By analyzing the co-occurrence of
autoplay and monetization in popular Android apps, including multiple YouTube apps,
we aim to understand their correlations and potential impact on user data and market
behavior. Our findings indicate a concerning prevalence of autoplay, often tied to
monetization, particularly in the paid version of YouTube where it is more common than
in the premium app. Notably, the use of autoplay in YouTube Premium may lead to a loss of
control over content for users who pay for the service, potentially creating an uneven
user experience. We also discovered that official YouTube apps have lower rates of autoplay
compared to third-party apps that use YouTube APIs, suggesting that providers may
strategically design their apps to minimize autonomy while keeping a competitive edge.
Lastly, we explore the broader market implications of these discoveries and outline some
recommendations to improve the industry's practices and protect user data and market
fairness.

The research investigates the Turing machine's capability to model complex systems, classifying behaviours as finitely executable or infinite, yet real-time executable. Finitely executable behaviours can be translated into the classical sense of Turing machine executability, whereas real-time executable behaviours are modelled by extended Turing machines operating within real-time constraints, where time is considered a distinct dimension. The study draws from the field of process calculus, focusing on the Pi-calculus, a framework for modelling communication and asynchrony in behaviours. The research demonstrates that, although extended Turing machines can simulate the Pi-calculus, the classical Turing machine falls short due to its inability to model certain asynchronous transitions. The study provides a characterisation of real-time executable Pi-calculus behaviours in terms of extended Turing machines.

A combinatorial Gray code represents all feasible combinations of a specific set of objects in sequence, changing one object at a time between adjacent configurations. In this study, we focus on a Gray code for set partitions initially proposed by Dichromatic. We introduce rules to create and verify valid set partitions and develop an algorithm to efficiently compute all feasible configurations and their corresponding Gray code. We also extend this concept to the set partitions with colored cycles and explore potential applications to the field of machine learning.

The sPHENIX experiment at RHIC is designed to study the fundamental structure of matter in high-energy quark-gluon plasma (QGP) studies, incorporating a rich scientific program spanning from soft to hard scattering processes. The experiment's robust particle identification capabilities, encompassing a wide range of mesons and baryons from light to heavy particles, as well as gluons, enables detailed observations of particle formation mechanisms across all energy levels. In addition to its core program, sPHENIX also offers tools for studying the behavior of heavy flavor quarks in high-energy environments and the structure of hadrons through electron-positron pair annihilation processes. The paper details the sPHENIX detector's design, the scientific goals of its research, and the current status of construction.

This study builds upon an existing time-series discretization approach that utilizes the isogeometric analysis method within a hierarchical space-time framework. The framework itself is an adaptation of the hierarchical space-time method originally proposed by Deville et al. in 2006. The current research expands the technique to accommodate problems characterized by deforming domains, with a focus on achieving accurate spatial discretization within each time segment. To achieve this, a crucial step involves verifying that the spatial discretization of adjacent time layers is compatible and free of gaps, especially when dealing with scenarios featuring sudden domain expansion or contraction. The presented space-time approach ensures that solution accuracy is maintained across space and time, with numerical simulations serving to confirm these findings.

In a recent paper, the concept of the circular $k$-way flow index of a signed graph was introduced, which involves optimizing the total flow from a starting vertex to other vertices through paths with specific properties in the signed graph, with a particular sign assigned. A formula was developed to calculate this index directly, which has since been used to determine the flow values in certain types of signed graphs. We have now extended this work to investigate the flow values in specific types of signed graphs, and found formulas to calculate them.

The Modular Subset Sum problem involves determining whether a subset of integers exists that equals a target value modulo m, from a given set of integers. A Monte-Carlo randomized algorithm solves this problem in O(n + m) time, on average, by utilizing a data structure known as a randomized ordered tree. This algorithm's performance is probabilistic, requiring O(n^2 + m*ln(m)) time in the worst case scenario.

Our research focuses on the Hα chromospheric activity of nearby M-type stars that are similar in size to the star Proxima Centauri. The Hα emission in these stars is crucial for understanding the characteristics of the star Proxima Centauri. We analyzed 13 nearby M dwarfs using the 2.5m MRO telescope and its AFOS spectrometer, which captured 1.1 square degrees of the sky around Proxima Centauri. We observed 57 flaring stars, which were classified into three categories based on their flare energy. We found that 22% of the stars in our sample are flaring stars, which is consistent with previous findings. We also discovered that flaring stars exhibit a specific range of Hα equivalent width, between -3. and 5.5 angstroms. Furthermore, our study shows that flares on these stars can occur rapidly, within 30 minutes, and that the flares observed in this study were of the order of 10^-3 of the star's Hα flux.
